newsitem.title: UK: CBOT rethinks trading link with LIFFE - paper.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rethinks trading link with LIFFE - paper.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) is reconsidering its partnership with the London International Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE), the Financial Times said on Monday.
The link, which is due to start on May 9, would offer LIFFE the exclusive right to trade the U.S. Treasury bond futures contracts when the Chicago trading floor is closed.
But some Chicago traders want the CBOT's electronic trading system to trade at the same time as LIFFE's U.S. Treasury bond futures session, the Financial Times (FT) said.
The CBOT members are wondering why trading in Chicago contracts should shift to London each night when it can be done electronically in the U.S., the newspaper added.
It reported that CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor had informal talks on the subject with LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson.
Arbor would soon come up with a formal proposal to alter the linkage agreement with LIFFE, the FT said.
The CBOT's electronic trading system took off last year after the Chicago and London futures exchanges had agreed their link in 1994.
The current agreement between the CBOT and LIFFE requires computer trading to be scaled back and then closed as the floor session develops, the FT said.
